stories.headline: Experimental drug alleviates symptoms of Huntington's disease The hereditary disorder Huntington's disease has so far been considered incurable. Its clinical manifestations include impaired motor control and psychiatric sy
stories.summary: Huntington's disease, a rare genetic disorder, causes progressive degeneration of nerve cells in the brain, leading to impaired motor control and psychiatric symptoms. The disease is characterized by a triad of symptoms: motor, cognitive, and psychiatric, with psychiatric symptoms often occurring before motor symptoms. Currently, there is no cure, but treatments can help manage symptoms. Medications such as antipsychotic drugs are used to address movement disorders associated with the disease. However, an experimental drug has shown promise in alleviating symptoms of Huntington's disease, offering potential hope for patients. The disease is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, resulting from an abnormal CAG triplet repeat expansion in the huntingtin gene. Further research is needed to understand the effectiveness of the experimental drug and its potential to improve the lives of those affected by this debilitating disease. Clinical trials are ongoing to assess its safety and efficacy.

stories.headline: Apple Releases iOS 26.6 Beta 3 and iPadOS 26.6 Beta 3 to Developers
stories.summary: Apple has released the third developer betas of iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, making them available for testing purposes. The updates come two weeks after the second betas were seeded to developers. Additionally, Apple has also rolled out the third betas of macOS Tahoe 26.6, watchOS 26.6, tvOS 26.6, and visionOS 26.6. These releases are part of the company's ongoing development cycle, with iOS 27 already available in developer beta. The new betas are intended for testing and debugging, allowing developers to prepare their apps for the upcoming updates. Meanwhile, Apple has also released iOS 26.5.2 to the public, providing a separate update for non-developer users. The latest betas are available to developers through the Apple Developer website and the Settings app on enrolled devices.

stories.headline: Meta Fury AI Glasses Review: The Worst Company Still Makes the Best Smart Glasses Meta's new smart glasses are like if "the worst person you know just made a really point" could be worn on your face.
stories.summary: Meta has released new smart glasses, including the Fury AI model, which offers improved features such as higher resolution and stabilization. The glasses come in three new styles, none of which are branded as "Ray-Ban." Despite concerns about the company, the Oakley Meta AI glasses are reported to fit comfortably and look less goofy than previous models. They may be more appealing to users, potentially making them more widely adopted. The new smart glasses could also be useful for applications such as ref cams, which could benefit from the improved footage quality. Meta's new smart glasses lineup has been reviewed, with some models receiving positive feedback for their design and functionality, despite reservations about the company itself. The glasses' capabilities and comfort make them a notable release in the smart glasses market.

stories.headline: Dbrand refunds Companion Cube Steam Machine case orders after Valve legal request dbrand is refunding all Steam Machine Companion Cube orders after confirming it had no Valve license. The company says Valve requested a takedown after launch.
stories.summary: Dbrand is refunding all orders for its Steam Machine Companion Cube case after receiving a legal request from Valve. The company confirmed it did not have a license from Valve to produce the Portal-themed accessory. Valve's legal team contacted dbrand, prompting the company to cancel the product and issue full refunds to customers. The Companion Cube case was designed as a custom enclosure for Steam Machines, but its production and sale were not authorized by Valve. As a result, dbrand is taking steps to comply with Valve's request, including cancelling all orders and providing refunds. The company had launched the product without obtaining the necessary permission from Valve, leading to the takedown request.

stories.headline: RB Leipzig chief denies Yan Diomande will join PSG despite claims summer transfer is close
stories.summary: RB Leipzig chief Marcel Schafer has denied that Yan Diomande will join Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) this summer, despite reports suggesting a transfer is close. The 19-year-old Ivory Coast winger has attracted interest from top clubs, including Liverpool and PSG, after a breakout season in the Bundesliga and a strong performance at the FIFA World Cup. RB Leipzig has stated they have no intention of selling Diomande, valuing him at £100 million. The club has issued a public statement to clarify their stance on the player's future, amid growing speculation about his potential transfer. Diomande's impressive form has made him a target for several European clubs, but RB Leipzig is determined to keep him.

stories.headline: Hull KR's Pangai Junior handed six-match ban
stories.summary: Hull KR forward Tevita Pangai Junior has been banned for six matches and fined by the Rugby Football League (RFL) for gouging. The incident occurred during the team's loss to Leeds Rhinos at Headingley last Friday. Pangai Junior was found guilty of gouging a Leeds Rhinos player and will miss the next six matches, starting with the upcoming derby at Magic Weekend. The suspension is a significant blow to Hull KR, removing a key player from their short-term plans and creating selection pressure for the next six fixtures. The RFL's Match Review Panel handed down the six-match ban, which will keep Pangai Junior sidelined for a prolonged period. The ban is one of four suspensions given to Super League players by the RFL's Match Review Panel.

stories.headline: Ticket Prices Plunge for World Cup Knockout Matches
stories.summary: Ticket prices for World Cup knockout matches have significantly decreased. The cost of resale tickets for the USMNT's July 2 game against Bosnia and Herzegovina has dropped to $1,650, down from $2,705 on June 22. Round-of-32 prices have fallen almost 40% in the past week. According to TicketData.com, the median get-in price for the remaining 31 matches is $1,730, a 41% decrease over the past week. The cheapest available tickets have slid across nearly every remaining fixture. Previously, the get-in price for a round of 32 match in Santa Clara, California, on July 1, featuring the US team, had jumped above $3,000. The decline in ticket prices may indicate a shift in demand as the tournament progresses. Ticket prices continue to fluctuate on resale sites.

stories.headline: CTE poses a massive dilemma for the AFL, Experts say urgent action is needed to protect players
stories.summary: The Australian Football League (AFL) is facing a significant dilemma due to the growing concern of Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy (CTE), a brain disease linked to repeated head impacts. Recent cases, including the posthumous diagnosis of West Coast Eagles champion Adam Hunter, have highlighted the issue. Experts emphasize that CTE risk is driven by exposure to repeated head impacts, not just concussions. The AFL is currently battling a class action lawsuit brought by former Geelong player Max Rooke, who alleges the league was negligent in handling concussions, resulting in permanent injuries. With CTE only diagnosable after death, urgent action is needed to protect players' health and welfare, prompting calls for the AFL to take immediate measures to address the issue and prevent further cases. The league's response will be crucial in mitigating the risk of CTE among its players.

stories.headline: The Guardian: ‘It’s open green space versus construction’: Delhi’s historic polo club and the battle for the city’s future
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court is hearing a case regarding the Centre's plan to take over the Delhi Polo Club land for construction purposes. The court has expressed concerns about the loss of open green space, which helps reduce heat stress and support urban biodiversity. The Centre claims the land is needed for public and defence purposes, citing limited space in central Delhi. However, the court has questioned whether this would lead to further construction and high-rise buildings, contributing to the disappearance of green spaces in the city. The Indian Polo Association has challenged an eviction order and sought a stay. The court has asked the Centre to disclose its plans for the heritage structures on the premises and the intended use of the land, highlighting the need to preserve Delhi's remaining green areas.

stories.headline: The Hindu: Congress seeks Rajnath Singh’s resignation in controversy over Operation Sindoor deaths
stories.summary: The Congress party is seeking the resignation of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh over the controversy surrounding Operation Sindoor, a military operation that resulted in the deaths of six personnel in May 2025. The party alleges that the government concealed the deaths and denied the soldiers due honour. The Congress claims that Singh insulted the fallen soldiers and misled Parliament during a debate on the operation. The party has also sought a privilege motion against the Defence Minister, accusing him of providing false information. The controversy has sparked a political storm in India, with the Opposition demanding transparency and accountability from the government regarding the operation and the handling of the soldiers' deaths. The government's delay in disclosing the information, taking 13 months to do so, has added to the criticism.

stories.headline: The Hindu: Maharashtra TET paper leak points to an inter-State racket, finds investigation team
stories.summary: The Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) paper leak case has been found to be part of an inter-State racket, according to the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the matter. Three people have been arrested, with two hailing from Bihar and one from Haryana. The SIT has dispatched four teams to different states to investigate the alleged interstate examination paper leak network. The police have informed the court that the case involves an interstate syndicate engaged in leaking confidential examination papers for financial gain. The kingpin of the leak has been identified as a man from Bihar. The investigation has expanded beyond Maharashtra, with teams tracing the network in four states. The accused have been sent to police custody as the probe continues to uncover the extent of the inter-State racket.

stories.headline: India Today: Chinese encroachment in Arunachal? Indian Army calls reports incorrect
stories.summary: The Indian Army has denied reports of Chinese encroachment in Arunachal Pradesh, calling the claims "incorrect". The rebuttal came after a local group, representing the Nah tribal community, alleged that the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) had set up camps in the region. The group claimed that Chinese presence had gradually expanded in the area over the past 10-15 years. However, the Indian Army has firmly denied these reports, stating that there is no truth to the allegations of Chinese incursions in Arunachal Pradesh. The Army's denial comes amid ongoing tensions between India and China along their disputed border. The Indian Army has assured that it is monitoring the situation and is committed to protecting the country's territorial integrity. The denial has been reiterated by the Army in multiple statements over the past day.

stories.headline: Bitcoin ETFs Face Record $4.1 Billion June Outflow US Bitcoin funds see their largest monthly withdrawals since launching, as Bitcoin falls more than 18% in June.
stories.summary: US-listed Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) experienced a record $4.1 billion outflow in June, the largest monthly withdrawal since their launch in January 2024. According to Bloomberg-compiled data, investors pulled more than $4.1 billion from the 13 funds, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for $3 billion of the outflows. This significant withdrawal comes as Bitcoin's value fell more than 18% in June. The outflow suggests that traditional investors may be adopting a more defensive stance. The $4.1 billion outflow marks the worst month for US-listed spot Bitcoin ETFs, indicating a notable shift in investor sentiment amidst the decline in Bitcoin's value.

stories.headline: Casey's General Stores plans to add 400 locations in new three-year push Casey's General Stores plans to add at least 400 locations over the next three years as the convenience chain expands its prepared food business and invests in
stories.summary: Casey's General Stores plans to add at least 400 locations over the next three years through acquisitions and new builds. The company, which operates over 2,900 convenience stores, aims to expand its prepared food business and strengthen its food and beverage range. The new three-year strategy focuses on three main areas, with a emphasis on towns with populations under 20,000. Casey's is the nation's third-largest convenience store retailer and fifth-largest pizza chain. The expansion plan was unveiled at the company's 2026 Investor Day in New York City, where executives also reported a 65.5% surge in net income to $162.7 million in the quarter ended April 30. The new stores will be added in small towns, a market where Casey's has a strong presence, particularly in its home state of Iowa. The expansion is expected to further solidify the company's position in the market.

stories.headline: QuantRate Launches Free AI Crypto Trading Bot for 24/7 Bitcoin Market Monitoring QuantRate launches a free AI crypto trading bot that helps users monitor Bitcoin and digital asset markets around the clock, review AI-assisted signals and mana
stories.summary: QuantRate has launched a free AI crypto trading bot that provides 24/7 monitoring of Bitcoin and selected digital asset markets. The bot reviews AI-assisted signals based on volatility, price behavior, and strategy rules, allowing users to make informed trading decisions. This automated trading tool uses algorithms and strategies to execute trades, enabling traders to automate their trading strategies and monitor market movements around the clock. The launch of this free AI crypto trading bot aims to help users trade smarter and manage risk in the 24/7 crypto market. With no coding required, users can set up the bot in minutes and start trading with ease. The bot is part of a growing trend of AI-powered trading tools that are changing the way traders interact with the crypto market.

stories.headline: B.C. natural gas leak caused by crews hitting misidentified pipeline: TSB report A federal investigation has found the puncture of a natural gas pipeline in northeastern B.C. last November was caused by inaccurate identification of the pipel
stories.summary: A federal investigation found that a natural gas pipeline puncture in northeastern British Columbia last November was caused by inaccurate identification of the pipeline's location by crews. The incident occurred during construction activities, highlighting the importance of accurate pipeline mapping and identification. The Transportation Safety Board of Canada (TSB) conducted the investigation, which aimed to determine the cause of the leak. The puncture of the pipeline led to a gas leak, which posed safety risks to the surrounding area. The TSB report's findings will likely inform measures to prevent similar incidents in the future. The incident underscores the need for precise pipeline location identification to ensure safe construction and maintenance activities.

stories.headline: STARTRADER Launches Pre-IPO Trading Products for OpenAI and Anthropic The new CFD instruments give traders early exposure to two of the world's most prominent artificial intelligence companies ahead of anticipated public listings.
stories.summary: STARTRADER, a global multi-asset broker, has launched two new pre-IPO contracts for difference (CFD) products, OPENAIUSD (OpenAI) and ANTHUSD (Anthropic). The products are available for trading as of June 29, 2026, allowing traders to gain early exposure to two prominent artificial intelligence companies ahead of their anticipated public listings. The CFD instruments provide an opportunity for traders to speculate on the potential value of OpenAI and Anthropic before they go public. STARTRADER's launch of these products is aimed at giving traders a head start in the market, enabling them to capitalize on the growing interest in AI companies. The products are now available for trading on STARTRADER's platform, providing traders with a new investment opportunity in the emerging AI sector.

stories.headline: Anthropic, OpenAI Tax-Exempt IPO Move to Stoke Congress’ Ire The founders of major artificial intelligence companies have pledged to give away most of their wealth. Congress isn’t thrilled about it.
stories.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI, creators of AI models, plan to go public as soon as October. The founders have pledged to donate portions of company stock, giving away most of their wealth. This move is expected to spark a significant payday for AI investors. However, Congress is not pleased with the tax-exempt nature of the planned initial public offerings (IPOs). The founders' decision to donate their wealth is seen as a way to avoid taxes, which has raised concerns among lawmakers. The expected IPOs of OpenAI and Anthropic follow SpaceX's move to go public, potentially setting a new trend in the tech industry. The donations are part of the founders' philanthropic efforts, but the tax implications have caught the attention of Congress, which may lead to further scrutiny and potential regulatory actions.
